verification.canonical: art rows 7608-8700: 2.528/255, via `node scripts/sheet-shot.mjs` then `python3 scripts/band-diff.py 7608 8700`. Art rows start at 7608 (2594:462/463 hang 92 rows above the band) and stop at 8700; the last 49 rows are bare paper.
verification.sheetCheck: This band takes the sheet to exactly 8749, Frame 242's own height. That is the strongest single check in the project: it only lands if all twelve band heights are right, and a band off by one pixel would still diff clean on its own. scripts/check-footer.mjs asserts it.
verification.offline: The offline solve window 7600-8749 with the 6 text masks scores 2.875 -- that is what the placement work optimised, with the sliced photo plate composited and no live copy. Not comparable to the 2.528 figure.
verification.method: worth probe, then a global local refine on the ART-ROWS objective, then locate.py as a cross-check. Two layers were placed by the refine against the probe, and one by the clip rule against both -- see the individual notes.
verification.findings: Eight right-side layers (463, 466, 472, 292, 216, 212, 478, and 214) sit at exactly `375 - exportWidth`. Their declared x puts them partly or wholly off-frame -- 2594:463 declares x 409, past the frame entirely -- while the export came back unclipped, so that value is an upper BOUND from the clip rule, and the probe chose exactly it in every case. Four left-side layers land at or within 3px of x 0 for the mirror reason. So on this band the clip rule did more placement work than the probe did.
verification.textFindings: Six of the eight TEXT nodes sit at their node y exactly (178, 839, 887, 919 band-local, plus the three vendor lines which share 919). The two that do not are the two Pinyon Script blocks, and for the same reason as the wish band's heading: Figma reports NO lineHeight for either and both live in boxes taller than one line, so the line is centred inside the box. 2594:436 sweeps to 129 against node 127; 2594:295 to 268 against node 266. Both sharp.
verification.sweepPitfall: The first sweep of `.footer__body` read 7.05 at its own winner. `.footer__body--credit` carries BOTH classes, so `top: N !important` moved the bottom paragraph into the top paragraph's rows and scored two paragraphs on top of each other. Re-run as `.footer__body:not(.footer__body--credit)` it reads 2.75. Sweep selectors must not match a second element.
verification.unshipped: 2594:479 and 2594:480 ("mutiara last page") exported blank and rows 7620-7800 of the render carry no pearls, which confirms the drop. Group 176's own 714x216 export wraps four TEXT nodes and was deleted; only its two buttons survive as g176_2594-445_ig and g176_2594-449_wa. 2594:474 is byte-identical to 2594:473 and reuses it.
verification.live: Four things in this band are data, not art: 2594:208 is the couple's PHOTOGRAPH (bound to wedding.image_cover with the sliced plate as fallback and object-fit: cover, since a live photo has its own aspect); 2594:295 is their names, from pengantin; and the two credit buttons are links. HeroSection imports the same photo file directly and does NOT bind the API -- a pre-existing gap, recorded but not fixed here.
verification.deviations: The design's own footer line reads "Antonio + Aliyah" where the bride is "Ayu Shella Pratni (Allysa)" -- an inconsistency in the design. Live names win, so those text rows never diff clean once pengantin is populated; the design's literal is the unconfigured fallback. The WhatsApp button has no number anywhere in the design or the production app, and a wa.me/ with no number is a dead link, so it renders as inert art unless wedding.vendor_whatsapp is set -- the same call the akad band's Maps button makes. Both Pinyon blocks are centred on their own box centres rather than left-aligned as declared, so a longer live name stays put.
